chunks: It is narrated by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah and Ṣafwān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked him about a man afflicted with sores that continue to bleed without stopping: how should he perform salat (prayer)? He said: He should perform salat (prayer), even if the blood is flowing.

key_terms.الدِّمَاءُ: bloods, meaning the blood flowing from the wounds
key_terms.الْقُرُوحُ: sores or wounds afflicting the body

ai.seo_question: How should a person pray if his wounds keep bleeding continuously?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person whose sores continue bleeding and do not cease. It indicates that such a person should still perform salat (prayer) despite the ongoing flow of blood, showing a ruling of concession in a case of continuous bleeding.
